query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: On-the-fly active-learning machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can replace full ab initio molecular-dynamics (AIMD) in thermodynamic integration workflows to yield fusion free energies and high-temperature thermodynamic properties of metallic systems with <5% error at an order-of-magnitude lower computational cost.
generation.material_initial_state: Elemental (Al, Ni) and binary (NiAl) metals in both solid (fcc, B2) and liquid phases near their melting points.
generation.intervention: Implement an on-the-fly active-learning scheme (e.g. Gaussian approximation or neural-network potential) during brief AIMD runs at key temperatures to train an MLIP, then use the MLIP to carry out long molecular-dynamics based thermodynamic integration for free-energy differences.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure; temperatures from 0.8 Tm to 1.2 Tm; compositions: pure Al, pure Ni, equiatomic NiAl.
generation.structural_mediator: The trained MLIP surrogate for the ab initio potential-energy surface.
generation.mechanism: MLIP captures anharmonic vibrations and electron–phonon coupling by reproducing ab initio forces and energies across sampled configurations, enabling extensive MD sampling for vibrational entropy and free-energy integration at low cost.
generation.predicted_outcome: For elemental and binary systems: fusion free energies within 5% (≈0.02 eV/atom) of AIMD thermodynamic integration, at ≈10 × speed-up over direct AIMD workflows and ≈5 × over TOR-TILD for NiAl.
generation.baseline: Direct AIMD-based thermodynamic integration (explicit free-energy evaluation) and TOR-TILD for binaries.
generation.boundary: Valid for up to two-component metallic alloys under ambient pressure; temperature range 0.8–1.2 Tm.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty on MLIP transferability may be ±10–20% in free-energy differences when extrapolated; composition complexity beyond binaries not yet tested.

falsification_experiment.design: Compute melting free energies (ΔG_s→l), latent heat, and melting temperature for pure Al and equiatomic NiAl using (a) direct AIMD thermodynamic integration, (b) the proposed MLIP-based TI workflow, and (c) TOR-TILD (for NiAl). All under identical P–T conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If MLIP-based TI yields melting temperatures deviating by >10 K or latent heats differing by >0.1 kJ/mol compared to direct AIMD TI, or if its wall-time speed-up is <5× relative to TOR-TILD on NiAl, the hypothesis is falsified.
